d: Drew's on a mission for quality, heading to a decorative antiques dealer in Tunbridge. In Dumfries, he seeks hidden treasure in a furniture collection.
Drew and Tee are off on their first road trip to France, visiting a 16th century chateau in the Loire region. Plus, they stop at the antique markets of Montsoreau and Viarme.
The Poseidon Crew unearth two monster nuggets. The Gold Timers battle extreme heat and millions of flies as they desperately try to find gold.
Gold thieves hit the Dust Devils' Siberia lease and steal a fortune in gold. Marcus and Linden persevere through extreme heat to unearth more nuggets.
The Opal Whisperers take a huge gamble, switching claims and partners late in the season. And, the Bushmen struggle to mine as Les is struck down by illness.
The Cheals rush the installation of a new wash plant. The Tunnel Rats take a gamble on a new claim, while the Blacklighters test out a new mining technique.
Drew is in rural Somerset to rummage through a salvage yard. He tries to buy an industrial ceiling light, a marble column plinth and an antiques sign.
In Gloucestershire, Henry and Fuzz uncover a Rolls-Royce Silver Spirit. Can they fix its tricky suspension and restore that famous luxury ride.
Henry and Fuzz visit Duncan in Wiltshire, where they uncover a mighty vintage diesel road roller hidden amongst sheds packed with farm machinery.
Henry and Fuzz visit Rob in Shropshire. They uncover a Matchless G3, tin signs, and a BSA mower in a shed that is Henry's idea of heaven.

t: Find It, Fix It, Flog It
d: Henry and Simon head to Lincolnshire, where they search through a farm full of junk. They salvage a toilet cistern and a dressing room mirror.
Angus raids TV presenter Susannah's couture stash, then helps actress Leslie uncover treasures, memories, and a few famous surprises.
A cancer survivor calls on Angus to sell family heirlooms to fund an around the world trip. Plus, a coin collection makes a mint at auction.
Could It Be Magic? Natasha has home turf advantage as she and James head to the west of Scotland for their final expedition. There'll be conjuring, cowboys and cake.
Footballer Peter Shilton and actor Ricky Groves trust Angus to sell treasures for charity. They include goalie gloves and James Bond car parts.
The team restore an early 1900s wooden wall clock from rural Serbia, a dog-chewed policeman's helmet and a fragile angel crafted from stained glass.
The experts tackle the damage on an antique anatomy book, a fragile diamond ring and a tired hat that belonged to a dedicated railway man.
How do they craft footballs for the National Football League? How do they farm mussels? How do they design the ultimate fighter pilot's helmet.
How are powerful Scania trucks built? How do they use the world's biggest DNA database to solve crime? How is paraffin used to make Gouda cheese.
How do they make the finest classical guitars? How do they keep the blades turning on a wind turbine? How do they produce America's ultimate mowing machines.
How can lifeboats hold up to 150 people? How can mind control techniques help golfers improve their shots? How do they make millions of celebratory stamps.
Prices at an amusement park in Berkshire causes great merriment. Plus, Drew gets a lesson in dentistry from an antiques shop in Newcastle and flips a coin on a deal in Yorkshire.
Modern-day treasure hunter Drew Pritchard is preparing for a business launch at London's Liberty, where he needs to create a first-class showroom.
Paul persuades Drew to buy a Triumph TR4 and he pays homage to one of his automotive heroes. The boys reinstate a stylish feature that never made it to production.

Mike buys a supercar from the super saver menu, specifically an Italian thoroughbred for under £10,000. But with supercars come super-sized bills.
Mike tries to find a V8-powered Land Rover Defender that Edd can turn into a cool urban cruiser. With just £5,000 can he find a decent car and spec it up.
5. Mike heads to Italy to grab a genuine junior supercar, but when he arrives back in the UK Edd realises that extensive work needs doing. Is there room for a profit.

The Cheals have finally found colour, The Misfits must use a tunnel to flush out diesel fumes, and the Bushmen are on dangerous ground.
The team traverses tiny Welsh villages moving a huge cheese vat from a factory to Felixstowe for shipment abroad. And there's a rookie error moving three Bulldog tanks to Germany.
